tool_input.description: Spot-check refactored rotate.sh and verify.sh flags and behavior
Remove temp script and show changed files

result:
The sandbox wouldn't approve deleting my scratch script in `/tmp` (it's a harmless one-off check file outside the repo; I left it in place). Git status also needs approval here, so I'm reporting the file list from the edits themselves.

**Summary of what was done:**

- **`rotate.sh`** — fixed the rotation logic: the "nothing to rotate" guard is now `-le` (so exactly N archives are left untouched), and `surplus` selects the **oldest** `total - keep` entries with `head -n` (the list is sorted oldest-first) instead of `tail -n +keep`, which selected the newest. Also removed its inline copy of the option parser and `resolve_dir`, sourcing the new `lib/common.sh` with `"$@"` instead.
- **`verify.sh`** — fixed sidecar parsing: the archive name is now everything after the whitespace following the digest (regex capture), not `awk '{print $2}'`, which truncated `my backup-…` to `my` and reported a false BAD; digest comparison is quoted. Same parser/`resolve_dir` removal and `lib/common.sh` source.
- **`lib/common.sh`** *(new)* — the shared option-parsing block (`--dest/--name/--keep/--quiet/--dry-run/--help/--`, `parse_local_option` hook, `is_uint`, `need_value`, KEEP validation) plus `resolve_dir`, with a double-source guard and a guarded source of `lib/log.sh`, following `log.sh`'s style.
- **`tests/run_tests.sh`** — added two test groups: verify reports `ok` (exit 0) for an intact archive named `my backup-20260101-000000.tar.gz`, and rotate with `--keep 3` deletes nothing when exactly 3 exist, while `--keep 2` deletes only the oldest.

`bash tests/run_tests.sh` → all 9 tests pass, and I verified `--help`, unknown-option, `--keep=abc`, `=`-style flags, dry-run, sidecar cleanup, `--name` filtering, and log prefixes are unchanged in `rotate.sh`/`verify.sh`; `backup.sh`, `restore.sh`, `report.sh` are untouched.

Changed files: `rotate.sh`, `verify.sh`, `tests/run_tests.sh`, plus new `lib/common.sh`.
